strings.account.title: My account
strings.account.profile.heading: Profile
strings.account.profile.email_hint: Used as the recipient address if a notification rule targets you (see Notifications). Not used for login.
strings.account.language.heading: Language
strings.account.language.label: UI language
strings.account.language.help: Only affects your own account — everyone else keeps their own choice (or the default, English).
strings.account.must_change_password: An administrator set this password — please change it below.
strings.account.totp.new_codes_notice: New recovery codes generated — the old ones no longer work.
strings.account.totp.save_codes_before: Save these recovery codes somewhere safe now —
strings.account.totp.save_codes_after: . Each one can be used once, in place of a code from your app, if you lose access to it.
strings.account.password.heading: Password
strings.account.totp.heading: Two-factor authentication
strings.account.totp.regen_label: Current code, to regenerate recovery codes
strings.account.totp.disable_label: Current code or a recovery code, to disable
strings.account.passkeys.heading: Passkeys
strings.account.passkeys.hint_before: A hardware security key, your device's own biometrics/PIN, or a password manager (Bitwarden, 1Password, your browser's own — pick it from the prompt "Add a passkey" opens) as a second factor alongside (or in place of) TOTP — see
strings.account.passkeys.hint_after: if you're not sure what this is.
strings.account.passkeys.remove_confirm: Remove this passkey? It will no longer be able to sign in to this account.
strings.account.sessions.hint: Signs out every other browser/device this account is logged into — not this one.
strings.account.sessions.confirm: Log out of every other session?
strings.totp_enroll.required_by_role: Your role requires two-factor authentication. You won't be able to use ucc until you finish enrolling it here.
strings.totp_enroll.scan_hint: Scan this with an authenticator app (Google Authenticator, Authy, 1Password, ...), or enter the setup key manually, then confirm with a code it generates.
strings.totp_challenge.title: Two-factor authentication
strings.totp_challenge.heading: Verify it's you
strings.totp_challenge.code_hint: Enter the 6-digit code from your authenticator app, or one of your recovery codes if you've lost access to it.
strings.totp_challenge.or_use_key: Or, use a security key or your device's biometrics instead:
strings.totp_challenge.sign_in_with_key: Sign in with a security key or your device's biometrics.
strings.dashboard.title: Dashboard
strings.dashboard.activity.heading: Recent activity
strings.dashboard.no_access: Your role doesn't have view access to any of the areas this dashboard summarizes.
strings.audit.title: Audit log
strings.audit.intro: Who (account and source IP), what happened, its outcome, and when. A blank "User" is a pre-login event (a failed login attempt) or an automatic job.
strings.audit.search.placeholder: Search by action, summary, target, IP...
strings.audit.export_hint: Export respects the filters above (blank means everything).
strings.audit.empty.match_filter: No audit log entries match this filter.
strings.audit.save_view.duplicate: You already have a saved view with that name.
strings.users.title: Users
strings.users.impersonate.confirm: Sign in as {name}? Everything done from then on is logged under their account until you log out.
strings.impersonation.banner_title: You're signed in as this account via Impersonate, started by {admin}. Log out to return to your own account.
strings.roles.title: Roles
strings.roles.table.name: Name
strings.roles.assigned_to: Assigned to {count} user(s) — reassign them before deleting this role.
strings.role.config_import.title: Import role configuration
strings.role.config_import.heading: Import role configuration
strings.role.config_import.hint1_after: ("Export config (JSON)"). This creates real roles directly, with their full permission set.
strings.role.config_import.hint2: A role whose name already exists is skipped, not overwritten — this never changes an existing role's permissions.
strings.role.config_import.unknown_permission_wa: These permission(s) aren't recognized on this instance (likely an older version than the one that exported this file) and were dropped from the imported role(s):
strings.users.delete_confirm: Delete user "{username}"? This cannot be undone.
strings.users.edit.password_hint: Leave blank to keep the existing password unchanged.
strings.users.edit.active_label: Active — unchecking immediately signs this user out everywhere
strings.users.edit.reset_password_hint: Sets a new password and signs this user out everywhere — they must change it on next login.
strings.users.edit.reset_password_confirm: Reset this user's password and sign them out everywhere?
strings.users.edit.temp_permissions_hint: A permission on top of whatever the account's role already grants — e.g. "terminal access for 2 hours" — that lapses on its own, no separate revoke step needed unless you want to end it early.
strings.users.edit.logout_confirm: Sign this user out of every session?
strings.roles.new.title: Add role
strings.roles.new.require_totp: Require two-factor authentication (TOTP) for users with this role
strings.roles.new.require_totp_hint: A user holding this role who hasn't enrolled TOTP is blocked from everything except enrolling it (and logging out) — checked live on every request, not just at login. Doesn't apply to OIDC accounts (their provider is expected to own MFA — TOTP isn't offered for them).
strings.users.new.title: Add user
strings.users.new.email_hint: Optional — the address notification rules send to when they target this user (see Notifications). Not used for login.
strings.users.new.username_hint: Lowercase letters, digits, '.', '_', '-'. This is also the LDAP username and the OIDC identity, if used.
strings.users.new.auth_provider_hint: "local": a password set below. "ldap"/"oidc": leave the password field empty — the username is matched against the directory/provider instead (see Settings).
strings.users.new.password_hint: At least 12 characters. Required for "local" accounts, left blank otherwise. The user must change it on first login.
strings.scheduling.run_enqueued: Run enqueued — check the Fabric page shortly.
strings.scheduling.target_hint: A disabled Fabric is skipped when the schedule fires.
strings.scheduling.target_restricted_hint: Your account is restricted to specific Fabrics, so "All Fabrics" isn't available as a target.
strings.scheduling.cron_hint: Standard 5-field cron: minute hour day-of-month month day-of-week, always interpreted in UTC. E.g.
strings.scheduling.history.title: Run history
strings.ai.title: AI assistant
strings.ai.intro_before_confirm: Describe what you want in plain language. The assistant can look up your Fabrics and devices with their firmware versions on its own. It cannot change anything.
strings.ai.intro_after_confirm: . It can only propose what your own role already allows you to do by hand.
strings.ai.model_hint: A conversation stays on the model it was started with.
strings.ai.first_message_placeholder: e.g. which access points have a firmware update available?
strings.ai.no_model_enabled: No AI model is enabled yet.
strings.ai.configure_provider_hint_before: Configure a provider, fetch its models, and tick the ones to allow on the
strings.ai.admin_needed_hint: An administrator needs to configure an AI provider in Settings first.
strings.ai.table.title: Title
strings.ai.privacy_hint_before: Conversations are private to your own account — nobody else, including administrators, can read them. Anything you actually confirm still shows up in the
strings.ai.chat.command_label: Command, exactly as it will run:
strings.ai.chat.read_before_confirming: Read the command and the target list above before confirming. Nothing has run yet.
strings.ai.chat.no_messages_yet: No messages yet — ask something below.
strings.ai.chat.message_placeholder: e.g. list the devices in Fabric Office
strings.ai.chat.waiting_for_reply: Waiting for the assistant's reply — this updates automatically.
strings.ai.chat.answers_can_take_a_while: Answers can take a little while when the assistant looks things up.
strings.settings.checks.background_checks_hint: How often every enabled Fabric is re-synced from UniFi Site Manager; a Fabric can override it on its edit page. Applies within a minute, no restart needed.
strings.settings.security.audit_hash_chain_hint: Every entry is hash-chained (each links to the previous one's hash), so altering or removing an entry breaks the chain from that point on — see Audit and the wiki page "Architecture" for how that works and what it doesn't protect against.
strings.settings.security.keep_audit_days_hint: Leave empty to keep every entry forever (the default). Otherwise, entries older than this are permanently deleted once a day — the chain's most recent entries and its ability to verify what remains are unaffected, since only the oldest end is ever pruned.
strings.settings.security.export_hint_before: Every entry can also be exported for archival/compliance outside the app:
strings.settings.security.export_hint_after: (the Audit page's own export links respect whatever search/outcome filter is set there).
strings.settings.integrations.syslog_hint: Live-mirrors every audit log entry to an external syslog server (e.g. a SIEM) as it's written — RFC 5424 formatted, best-effort: a delivery failure here is only ever logged, never blocks the action being audited. The database entry (exportable on the Security tab) is always the real record; this is just a copy sent elsewhere.
strings.settings.integrations.smtp_hint: Configuration only, for now — nothing in the app sends an email through this yet. Lets the relay be set up and saved ahead of an actual notification feature. Same encrypted-secret convention as LDAP/OIDC below.
strings.settings.integrations.ldap_hint_before: When enabled, a user set to login method "ldap" (see
strings.settings.integrations.ldap_hint_after: ) logs in with the same username/password form as a local account — the username is looked up in the directory below, and their password is checked against it, not against anything stored here.
strings.settings.integrations.use_starttls: Use StartTLS (only relevant for a plain "ldap://" server URI)
strings.settings.integrations.tls_verify_hint: Only for "ldaps://" or StartTLS. Turn off only if you know this directory's certificate is self-signed or otherwise won't validate and you still want to use it — with it off, any certificate is accepted, with no protection against a machine-in-the-middle.
strings.settings.integrations.leave_blank_hint: Leave blank to keep the current value unchanged.
strings.settings.integrations.user_search_filter: Must contain {username}. Typical OpenLDAP: (uid={username}). Active Directory: (sAMAccountName={username}).
strings.settings.integrations.provider_name_hint: Shown on the login button ("Log in with" + this name) instead of the generic "OIDC" — purely cosmetic, e.g. "Entra ID", "Authentik", "Google Workspace". Blank keeps the generic label.
strings.settings.integrations.oidc_hint_before: When enabled, the login page shows a "Log in with OIDC" button. A user set to login method "oidc" (see
strings.settings.integrations.oidc_hint_after: ) is matched by comparing their username against the claim named below in the ID token the provider returns — nothing is auto-created from this.
strings.settings.integrations.issuer_url_hint: Must serve /.well-known/openid-configuration (standard for any OIDC provider — Keycloak, Authentik, Entra ID, Okta, Google, ...).
strings.settings.ai.intro_after: page. Enabling a provider isn't the same as trusting its whole catalog: fetch its models, then tick exactly which ones may be picked for a conversation. Everything the assistant can actually do against a machine is still gated by the requesting user's own role permissions, and every action it proposes must be confirmed by a human before it runs.
strings.settings.ai.base_url_hint: Required when this provider is enabled. Must expose the OpenAI /models and /chat/completions endpoints.
strings.settings.ai.token_limits_hint_before: Global ceilings on total tokens (input + output, all providers together) spent by the AI assistant in a
strings.settings.ai.token_limits_hint_after: window — the last 24 hours, 7 days, and 30 days respectively, not calendar days/weeks/months. A limit that is already reached blocks the next chat turn before any provider call is made. Leave empty for no limit.
strings.notifications.title: Notifications
strings.notifications.history.title: Notification history
strings.notifications.history.hint: The last 200 delivery attempts (email or webhook), newest first — real sends and test sends alike.
strings.notifications.history.empty: No notifications have been sent yet.
strings.notifications.smtp_not_configured: No SMTP relay is configured, so notification emails won't actually send yet.
strings.notifications.table.name: Name
strings.notifications.rule.trigger_hint: Fires on any of the checked events.
strings.notifications.rule.template_hint_before: Pick a custom template instead of the built-in one for the event that fired. Manage templates on the
strings.notifications.rule.send_via_hint: Email uses the recipients/roles below; a webhook posts JSON to a URL instead and ignores them.
strings.notifications.rule.webhook_url_hint: A JSON POST is sent here on every match — include any auth token in the URL itself (e.g. a Slack/Discord incoming webhook link).
strings.notifications.rule.send_test_hint: Sends one test message through this rule's own channel/template — email goes only to you, never the rule's real recipients.
strings.notifications.rule.view_history: View delivery history for this rule
strings.notifications.rule.test_sent: Test notification sent — check your inbox (or the History page).
strings.notifications.rule.recipients_hint: A recipient is anyone listed directly above, or any active account holding one of the roles above.
strings.notifications.rule.scope_hint: Leave all unchecked to match every Fabric. Ticking one or more limits this rule to those Fabrics only.
strings.notifications.templates.title: Email templates
strings.notifications.templates.hint: One template per event, used to render the subject/body of a notification email. An event with no customized template uses the built-in default shown here.
strings.notifications.templates.table.subject: Subject
strings.notifications.templates.table.name: Name
strings.notifications.templates.custom_hint: A named template any rule can pick instead of the per-event one above — see a rule's Delivery section.
strings.notifications.template.title: Template: {event}
strings.notifications.template.body_hint: Plain text. Available placeholders: {event}, {timestamp}, {fabric_name}, {target_name}, {product}, {version}, {risk_level}, {max_risk_level}, {details}. An unrecognized placeholder is left as literal text.
strings.notifications.template.reset_confirm: Reset this template to the built-in default? Your customized text will be lost.
strings.notifications.rule.import_hint: Paste a rule (or a YAML list of several) exported from this or another ucc instance. A rule is matched by name — importing one that already exists updates it in place; a new name creates a new rule.
strings.settings.checks.notification_log_hint: One row per actual send attempt (email or webhook), kept for troubleshooting on the Notifications → History page.
strings.dashboard.stats.consoles_with_update: Consoles with a UniFi OS update
strings.fabrics.none_yet: No Fabrics yet. Add one with a UniFi Site Manager API key (unifi.ui.com → API).
strings.fabrics.no_consoles: Nothing synced yet — the first sync runs right after the Fabric is added.
strings.fabrics.sync_queued: Sync queued — this page refreshes when it finishes.
strings.fabrics.table.name: Name
strings.fabrics.form.api_key_hint: Create one at unifi.ui.com → API. It is checked against Site Manager before saving and stored encrypted.
strings.fabrics.form.api_key_keep_hint: Leave blank to keep the current key. A new key is checked against Site Manager before saving.
strings.fabrics.form.enabled_hint: A disabled Fabric keeps its inventory but is skipped by the periodic sync and by scheduled tasks.
strings.fabrics.delete.heading: Delete Fabric
strings.fabrics.delete.hint: Removes the stored API key and everything synced under this Fabric. Nothing is changed on the UniFi side.
strings.fabrics.delete.confirm: Delete Fabric "{name}" and its synced inventory?
strings.users.new.restrict_fabrics_hint: Leave all unchecked for access to every Fabric. Checked Fabrics are the only ones this account can see.
strings.users.edit.restrict_fabrics_hint: Leave all unchecked for access to every Fabric. You can't change your own Fabric access.
strings.notifications.event.update_blocked: Update stopped by the AI risk level
strings.notifications.event.auto_update_risk: UniFi auto-update would install a STOP version
strings.fabrics.auto_update.warning: UniFi updates this console automatically (UniFi OS, {schedule}) — outside ucc's AI gate. Turn it off in UniFi if ucc should decide.
strings.fabrics.auto_update.warning_apps: UniFi updates this console and its applications automatically ({schedule}) — outside ucc's AI gate. Turn it off in UniFi if ucc should decide.
strings.fabrics.update_version_unknown_hint: Site Manager reports an update but not its version (often while the device is offline).
strings.fabrics.form.max_risk_hint: A pending update whose release is rated above this level is STOP for this Fabric (a console or device can override it in its own settings).
strings.fabrics.community_latest_hint: The console doesn't offer this update yet (UniFi rolls releases out gradually), but it is the newest public release on community.ui.com.
strings.releases.verdict.go_hint: The release's risk is within the acceptable level {max}/5, or it was allowed by hand.
strings.releases.verdict.stop_hint: The release's risk is above the acceptable level {max}/5. Someone with update.override can allow it.
strings.releases.verdict.pending_hint: The AI assessment has not finished, failed, or is turned off.
strings.releases.intro: Every release your consoles and devices could update to, rated 1 (stable) to 5 (broken) from the release notes and what people report on community.ui.com, Reddit and the web. Above the acceptable level ({level}/5 globally, overridable per Fabric) the recommendation is STOP. ucc only recommends — run updates in UniFi.
strings.releases.not_configured: Release assessment is off: choose an AI model in Settings → Assessments.
strings.releases.unknown_targets: {count} pending update(s) can't be rated: Site Manager says an update exists but not to which version.
strings.releases.manual_hint: The risk level was set by hand and replaces the AI's.
strings.releases.none: No pending updates — nothing to assess.
strings.releases.queued: The assessment is queued; this page shows the result once it finishes.
strings.releases.manual_by: Risk level {level}/5 set by hand by {user} on {when}.
strings.releases.allowed_by: Allowed by {user} on {when}: every pending update to this release is GO, whatever its risk level.
strings.releases.allow_hint: Allowing a release makes every pending update to it GO, whatever its risk level. Recorded in the audit log.
strings.releases.affected_none: No console or device you can see has a pending update to this release.
strings.settings.releases.title: Release assessment
strings.settings.releases.intro: ucc rates every release a synced console or device could update to, from 1 (stable) to 5 (broken), and recommends GO or STOP against the acceptable level. It never runs updates itself.
strings.settings.releases.max_risk_hint: Above this level a pending update is STOP. Each Fabric can override it on its edit page.
strings.settings.releases.model_hint: Any model enabled on the AI tab. Assessments count toward the AI token limits.
strings.settings.releases.community_hint: community.ui.com (release notes, their comments, forum questions) is always read; it needs no account.
strings.settings.releases.reddit_hint: Reddit answers API calls only with an app's credentials: create a "script" app at reddit.com/prefs/apps (free, no account access is used). Leave empty to skip Reddit.
strings.settings.releases.web_hint: Finds reports outside community.ui.com and Reddit. SearXNG needs its JSON output enabled (search.formats: [html, json]).
strings.catalog.intro: The newest versions of every UniFi application on community.ui.com, rated 1 (stable) to 5 (broken) like everything on Assessments — whether or not your consoles run them yet. Acceptable level: {level}/5.
strings.catalog.empty: No releases read from community.ui.com yet — the list is read when the beat service starts and then every day (Settings → Checks); “Refresh now” reads it right away.
strings.live.enable_hint: Get a browser notification when this page updates while backgrounded.
strings.live.on_hint: Click to turn off background notifications for this Fabric's page.
strings.live.blocked_hint: Blocked in this browser's site settings.
strings.fabrics.form.sync_interval_hint: How often this Fabric is synced from Site Manager. Empty = the global setting ({seconds} s).
strings.policy.title: Settings: {name}
strings.policy.scope.console: Console — applies to its UniFi OS and applications, not to the devices adopted on it
strings.policy.edit_hint: This one's own acceptable risk level and hidden release stages
strings.policy.own_hint: Has its own settings instead of the Fabric's
strings.policy.risk_hint: A pending update rated above this level is STOP here.
strings.policy.hidden_stages_hint: A release in a hidden stage is not listed, not offered as an update and not rated by the AI (no tokens spent). What already runs is still shown.
strings.releases.stage.GA: GA — General Availability: the stable release for everyone
strings.releases.stage.RC: RC — Release Candidate: nearly final, published for wider testing before GA
strings.releases.stage.T: T — Testing: an early build published for testing (often the first firmware of new hardware)
strings.releases.stage.U: U — Unstable: known to be unstable, or recalled
strings.releases.stage.unknown: Stage not known (no community.ui.com post found yet)
strings.releases.assess_all_hint: Re-assess now every release with a pending update below (one AI call per release — costs tokens)
strings.releases.assess_all_queued: Queued {count} assessments — the ratings update as they finish.
strings.settings.ai.choice_hint: The primary model rates releases and is preselected for new assistant conversations. When a call fails (a provider error, its timeout, or an answer that can't be used), the fallback model is tried.
strings.settings.ai.choice_none: Enable a provider and some of its models below first.
strings.settings.ai.fallback_hint: Best from another provider, so an outage of one doesn't stop both.
strings.settings.ai.fallback_used_hint: Answered by the fallback model after the first choice failed
strings.settings.ai.timeout_hint: How long one request to this provider may take before it counts as failed and the fallback model is tried ({min}–{max} s).
strings.settings.ai.usage_hint: Tokens spent on release assessments and the assistant. Each call is also in the audit log (release.assess, ai.turn) with its tokens and duration.
strings.settings.releases.model_moved: The model that rates releases (primary and fallback) is set in
strings.catalog.more_hint: The full assessment: summary, every problem found, all sources, rating history and which of your consoles/devices it concerns.
strings.releases.context.general_hint: In general {level}/5 — lower here, because some of its problems hit hardware this one doesn't have
strings.releases.context.base: Risk {base}/5 where none of the hardware-specific problems apply, {level}/5 in general — each console and device is judged by what it actually has.
strings.fabrics.installed_risk_hint: The version running now is rated above the acceptable level {max}/5 for this hardware — see why, and whether a newer version is GO.
strings.fabrics.auto_update.risk: UniFi's own auto-update ({schedule}) would install a version ucc rates STOP — ucc can't stop it. Turn the auto-update off in UniFi, or accept the risk:
strings.releases.affects_hint: What the AI says this problem hits; consoles and devices without it are rated without this problem.
strings.releases.history.empty: No history yet — it starts with the next assessment.
strings.status.intro: Is the background machinery working: the periodic jobs, the worker, inventory syncs and release assessments.
strings.status.jobs_hint: Recorded since 0.3.0. The inventory sync intervals apply within a minute; a changed catalogue interval after a beat restart.
strings.releases.reports_hint: Independent reports the AI counted across community.ui.com, Reddit and the web — one is an anecdote, several weigh more.
strings.settings.checks.release_catalog_interval: How often the Releases page re-reads community.ui.com. Default 24; also read at beat start and by “Refresh now”. A change needs a beat restart.
strings.catalog.refreshing: Refreshing from community.ui.com — reload in a minute. New versions are then queued for assessment.
